CHARACTERISED 2026-10-13 (#145), and not a defect. Two back-to-back capture runs of identical code differ in 15 of 75 images, so the churn is NOT cross-session only as this entry previously stated - the earlier '21 of 79 / cross-session only' wording was an overstatement drawn from a summary rather than a measurement, repeated three times by the agent before being checked. 12 of the 15 are motion frames sampled from an unfrozen CSS animation at wall-clock offsets (e2e/motion.spec.ts): non-reproducible by construction and not review evidence. For the remaining 3, measured on the content-stress detail at 1280x900 across a reload: geometry, scroll offset, scroll height, focus, document.fonts.status, theme and DPR are all IDENTICAL and only rendered pixels differ - 648 of 1,152,000 pixels (0.056%). The capture helper already fast-forwards animations and passes animations:'disabled' and caret:'hide', and the stylesheet declares no CSS transitions, so a mid-transition capture is ruled out. The residue is glyph rasterization/compositor variance, which e2e/determinism.spec.ts already decided to guard by comparing text, computed styles and geometry instead of bytes. Confirmed by measurement; that reasoning stands. Visual acceptance rests on that content guard plus human inspection, never on a pixel diff.
